subject: Certification contingency scenarios and intake asks
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@havensec.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Certification contingency scenarios and upfront asks

Hi Marissa,

We're lining up a FedRAMP pre-assessment (federal agency intake) and an ISO 27001 Stage 1 between late October and mid-November. Before we lock windows I have a few concrete asks so we can scope the intake properly: 

- Confirm the in-scope boundary for both programs (are we looking only at US regions or global?): list of regions/cloud accounts.
- PII/data classification: what categories of customer data are processed in-scope for the audit (esp. model inputs vs. logs)?
- Subservice providers: current list and SOC/SOC-equivalent status for major vendors.
- Evidence retention: typical retention periods for logs, backups, and configuration snapshots that you can provide as attestable artifacts.
- SIG / CAIQ: do you have a recent CAIQ filled out or a SIG baseline we can include?
- Sample window expectations and maximum sample sizes (we need to line up artifact pulls and test accounts).

Also: in past engagements auditors have asked for a contingency approach when small nonconformities are discovered — do you have an established contingency/exception process we can cite (temporary compensating controls, remediation window, or remediation letters)?

If helpful, we're happy to run a 1-hour scoping call this week. If you can send an inventory template we can start mapping evidence owners.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Principal Security Assessor
Haven Security

[Note: attaching formal audit intake worksheet in follow-up if needed]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@havensec.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Certification contingency scenarios and upfront asks

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. We're available for a scoping call Thursday or Friday; I'll propose times in a separate calendar invite. Quick answers and next steps below: 

- Boundary: initial preference is US-only (primary clusters in us-west-2 and us-east-1) — we can expand to EU upon request but that will add workload.
- PII: model inputs are by default tokenized and routed through ephemeral caches; we treat customer-provided PII as high-sensitivity and will map controls accordingly. We will include sanitized examples rather than raw prompt data where possible.
- Subservice providers: I'll attach our current control-owners template and a short vendor list; several providers have SOC2 reports (we'll note which).
- Retention: we typically retain audit-relevant logs for 13 months (config snapshots 12 months) — I'll confirm retention buckets and provide a retention matrix.
- CAIQ/SIG: we maintain a CAIQ baseline; Olga will take point on packaging the CAIQ and the SIG mapping.
- Sample window: please advise max sample size; our default assent is to support up to 250 artifacts per control area within a 2-week window, but we can negotiate.

I've attached an evidence-inventory-template.csv so your team can start tagging what you'll request. Internally I'm going to stand up a short intake sprint and assign owners.

If you can confirm the auditor's ideal sample window and whether they require raw prompt material, we can finalize sprint dates.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-inventory-template.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Certification contingency scenarios and upfront asks

Team — forwarding Haven's intake asks. Proposed plan and asks for owners: 

- Karthik: lead FedRAMP scoping (verify cloud region boundary, PII defs, fallback options if sample access is delayed).
- Mina: evidence assembly (logs, config snapshots, backups); prepare redaction plan and sanitized examples.
- Olga: CAIQ / SIG packaging and control mapping; confirm which subservice SOC packages we can include.
- Proposed intake sprint: Sep 22 — Oct 3 (2 weeks) to gather and stage artifacts. If Haven needs sooner we'll compress to a 1-week triage + 1-week pull.
- Contingency ask: auditors sometimes request temporary compensating controls when an artifact isn't immediately available. We should pre-author an exception memo and remediation timeline (30 days typical) — can we draft a template?

I've attached a one-page proposed-intake-sprint-plan for your review. Please reply with any blocking issues or if we should expand scope to EU for this engagement.

Original message from Haven quoted below.

[Attachment: proposed-intake-sprint-plan.md]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Certification contingency scenarios and upfront asks

Thanks Marissa — quick notes after an internal scan: 

- Regions: confirm US-only (us-west-2, us-east-1) for initial scope. We'll treat EU as out-of-scope unless Haven confirms federal EU requirement.
- Data types: for FedRAMP we should mark raw customer prompts as "sensitive operational input" and supply sanitized examples only. Our logs (access and inference logs) are in-scope; retention matrix attached.
- Subservice providers: list in the vendor register; three key providers (storage, telemetry, KMS) have SOC2 Type II; we'll attach their attestations where possible.
- Sample sizing: 250 artifacts/control is workable; escalate if auditors request >500. That would require a dedicated extraction job.
- Contingency approach: I propose we prepare a short "Temporary Exception & Remediation Commitment" memo (template attached) that: identifies missing artifact, explains compensating control, and commits to remediation within 30 days. Only GRC sign-off required; legal review if exceptions affect customer data.

Attachments included: control-owners-list.xlsx; retention-matrix.pdf; temp-exception-template.docx

If we can lock sprint start Sep 22, I'll pre-populate the control-owner sheet and reach out to infra teams for scheduled extraction windows. Also flagging one risk: for some archived snapshots we only have hashed indices older than 9 months — that may complicate evidence that requires raw config files. Suggest we triage those controls early.

— Karthik
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Confirming we will scope the pre-assessment to US-only for now and the auditors accept sanitized examples in lieu of raw prompts. Our target intake window is Sep 25 — Oct 6; please stage artifacts for the first 3 days of that window where possible (we'll use the remainder for validation).

We appreciate the proposed temporary exception memo approach — please send the template in the intake packet. Final ask: can you include a short statement in the intake packet that lists which subservice providers have current SOC2 attestations (name + report date)? That will speed our review.

If you can get the initial inventory uploaded to the Drive folder by Sep 24 EOD we should be on track. I'll send a calendar invite for an initial scoping call Friday at 10am PT.

Best,
